digest.component_or_area: rebar fsck and doctor commands; store recovery tooling
propositions: fsck detects and classifies dirty-tracker wedges into three kinds: tracked deletions of store artifacts restorable from HEAD, untracked regenerable compaction leftovers, and orphaned .tmp-event-* files; each class is reported as a distinct finding in text and JSON output with counts and paths.

doctor --repair heals dirty-tracker wedges using two non-reentrant write-lock windows: first window restores tracked deletions via git checkout and quarantines leftovers under reconverge-quarantine; second window (after lock release) invokes sync.reconverge to converge the store; .tmp-event-* files are left untouched.
A backup ref (refs/rebar-doctor/<utc-ts>) is recorded at the store HEAD before any mutation to provide an audit envelope; mutation is refused if the backup ref cannot be recorded.
File mutations (checkout-restore and quarantine-move) are non-destructive: deleted files are restored from HEAD, leftovers are moved to quarantine (preserving bytes), and no files are deleted.
